Definition: perhaps from the same as G260; a strap, i.e. (specially) the tie (of a sandal) or the lash (of a scourge):--latchet, thong.
BiblicalUsage: himás means latchet, thong. It occurs 4 times in all, and the passages I have picked — Mark, Luke, John, and Acts — show it in its plain sense. I read it as a word that does its work quietly, without dressing anything up.
TheologicalSignificance: What himás tells me is that John knew he was not worthy to untie the strap of the Lord’s shoe — and that is the right posture. I hold that reading it plainly keeps me honest about what God actually said.
Sources: Strong's Exhaustive Concordance (1890), via OpenScriptures Strong's Dictionary (CC BY-SA)
